What it is

The Customer is a sales-practice role-play agent. It plays a realistic K-12 school-district buyer, lets you run a full conversation, and then steps out of character to coach you on how it went. It is a sparring partner, not a script - you talk, it pushes back the way a real prospect would, and you get better with every rep.

How to access it

The Customer is a shared Claude.ai Project - no install or setup needed. Sign in at claude.ai with your STA account, open Projects, and pick The Customer. Start a new chat inside the Project and you are ready to practice. Each chat is its own practice session.

Who it plays

  • Dana Okafor, IT Director - the technical decision-maker who cares about integration, security, and support. Sharp and skeptical; will catch a bluff.
  • Kevin Pratt, Junior Tech - hands-on, lower authority, in over his head, needs things made simple. The best support-call practice.
  • Linda Vasquez, Business Manager - budget, ROI, and procurement timing. Translates everything into dollars and staff hours.
  • Sharon Bell, Front-Office Secretary - the day-to-day user who lives in the product and guards her morning routine.

What you can practice

  • Cold pitch and opening
  • Discovery questions
  • Objection handling
  • Support calls
  • Renewal conversations

How a session works

  1. Tell it the persona and scenario you want to practice (or ask it for a scenario - it has a bank of ready-made ones).
  2. Run the conversation - it stays in character and reacts like a real prospect. It will not break character or go easy on you mid-scene.
  3. When you are done, type /debrief for GROW-structured coaching or /scorecard for a nine-behavior practice scorecard. ("Step out" or "/pause" also end the role-play.)
  4. The scorecard appears in the chat - copy it out if you want to track your reps over time.
Two things to remember. It is not a real customer - nothing it says reflects an actual account. And the scorecard is practice feedback, not data - it measures how you handled the rep, not anyone's real buying intent.

Try starting with

"Play an IT Director at a mid-size district. I'm cold-calling about VirtuaTime. Be a little skeptical."
